ideas.description: Stack E044's 28 px middle stage onto the E045 tip. This combines a near-miss with a margin that can absorb it. The tip is E045 (commit bfcff33): bs 1536, 24 px bilinear antialiased whole images for epochs 0-1.5 then 32 px, 6.75 epochs total, SGD-group lr x1.5, head lr x2 with wd halved, Muon lr 0.16 mom 0.8, lookahead 0.97^5, brightness/contrast jitter, whitening bias trained in epoch 1 only. Make one change, ported from E044 (drafts/E044_res3_submission.py): 24 px for epochs 0-1.5 as now, then 28 px whole images (F.interpolate, antialias=True, inside the compiled GPU augment after flip, translate and jitter) for epochs 1.5-3.0, then 32 px for the last 3.75 epochs. Total epochs, bs and every step-indexed schedule stay unchanged, so the sample stream and lr values are identical to E045. A switch that falls mid-epoch uses the first part of that epoch's permutation at the old resolution and the rest at the new one. The 28 px graph's final pool is F.max_pool2d with a static kernel equal to its final map (expect 3x3). Do NOT use amax or flatten().max (E009). In build(), warm up the 28 px train step without whitening-bias grad at bs 1536, plus every partial-batch shape at both switches, using channels_last tensors in the exact timed layout (E035). Check that total build time stays under ~450 s (E044 took 232 s for 6 variants). If I060's 20 px first stage was kept first, apply this change to that commit instead and leave its first stage alone. Run debug_nan.py on the new graph and compare trial-0 with later-trial train times.
ideas.expected: Time 5.12-5.32 s, point ~5.22 s (-4.4% vs 5.464 s; E044 saved 4.4% against the same bs-1536 base). Accuracy 0.750-0.759, point ~0.7545 (E045 0.7568 minus E044's -0.23 pp). Feasible means a new best, margin ~0.15 pp. If it misses 0.753 by <=0.1 pp, keep the code path and pair it with the next accuracy gain (I058/I064). A drop >=0.45 pp means E044's cost was not additive with the head-lr gain (the gain was re-draw); then close the 28 px stage and refute H2.3.3 at this epoch count.

ideas.description: Cash in E045's head-lr margin as fewer epochs, which is the follow-up pre-registered in I053. Run this only if I061 (28 px stage) is infeasible. If I061 is kept with margin >=0.3 pp, apply it to that commit instead; otherwise skip. On E045, change only the length of the 32 px phase, from 5.25 to 5.0 epochs (6.5 total). Scale the lr, Muon and lookahead schedules to the new total step count. The 24 px stage stays at 1.5 epochs, measured in samples. The last quarter-epoch uses the first quarter of that epoch's permutation, as in E027. Add any new final partial-batch shape to the build() warmup with channels_last tensors in the exact timed layout.
ideas.expected: Time ~5.25 s (-3.9%, range -2.5% to -5%): about 0.21 s of 32 px training removed. Accuracy 0.750-0.758, point ~0.7539 (slope ~1.14 pp/epoch x 0.25 = -0.29 pp). Feasible means a new best and supports H1.7.3's head gain as real margin. Below 0.753 means E045's +0.18 pp was largely re-draw; then mark H1.7.3 refuted for knee purposes.

ideas.description: Explore whether translate-2 is too much regularization at ~6.75 epochs, a test H1.8.2 has never had. On the tip (E045, or I061's successor if it is kept), remove the translate-2 augmentation in every resolution stage. Keep the alternating flip and the brightness/contrast jitter exactly as now. If translate is implemented as pad-and-random-crop inside the compiled augment, replace it with the identity, so the augment graph gets simpler but tensor shapes do not change. Re-warm the augment graph in build() with channels_last tensors of the exact timed layout. Eval is unchanged.
ideas.expected: Accuracy -0.7 to +0.35 pp, point -0.15 pp: translate usually helps even in short airbench runs, but jitter and LS 0.2 already regularize. Time -0.1% to -0.5% (a cheaper augment). A gain >=0.2 pp supports H1.8.2 and banks ~0.2 epoch for a trim. A drop >=0.3 pp refutes it and closes the augmentation-strength axis; translate stays.

ideas.description: Test the SGD group's other untested lever, which I048 deferred until the head axis was read. Head x0.5 cost 0.41 pp (E039) and head x2 gained 0.18 pp (E045), so the SGD group looks under-driven rather than over-driven. On the tip, change only the BatchNorm-bias lr multiplier from x64 to x128, and keep lr*wd constant for the BN biases by halving their wd. The head lr (x2), whitening-bias lr, Muon, lookahead, LS, curriculum, jitter and epochs stay identical. The lr is a 0-d tensor, so nothing recompiles and no new shapes are needed.
ideas.expected: Accuracy -0.45 to +0.35 pp, point +0.03 pp (BN biases at x64 x1.5 already move fast; doubling them may destabilize the early high-lr phase). Time unchanged within +-1.5%. A gain >=0.25 pp supports H1.7.1 and banks ~0.25 epoch. A drop >=0.25 pp means x64 is at or above the optimum; then x32 is the only untested side. If the result is within +-0.2 pp, the BN-bias axis is flat and H1.7.1 is refuted except for the head.

ideas.description: Check whether the E007 autotune settings still earn their cost, now that build time is close to binding. E044 needed 232 s for 6 graph variants, and I061/I060/I057 each add more variants against the 600 s limit. Kernels autotuned on SXM may also not transfer to the PCIe judge. On the tip, change only the compile settings: compile with the default mode instead of 'max-autotune-no-cudagraphs', and leave torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark False. The math, shapes and warmup coverage stay the same; still warm up every timed graph in build() with channels_last tensors of the exact layout. Clear the Inductor cache before the run so no stale autotune choices are reused. Record build time.
ideas.expected: Time +0.2% to +2.5%, point +0.9% (~5.51 s); E007 measured -1.1%, within jitter. Accuracy identical up to re-draw (+-0.15 pp). Build time drops ~50-70%. A gap under 1.5% supports H2.5.1. If so, discard the run (it is not faster) but record default-mode compile as the fallback whenever a stacked curriculum or bs variant pushes build past ~450 s. A gap >=2% refutes H2.5.1, and autotuning stays.

drop.reason: Its point estimate is +0.1 pp for +1.5% time. At the current exchange rates (~0.05-0.08 pp per 1% for curriculum or batch-size cuts, ~0.12+ for epochs) it needs >=+0.2 pp just to break even. Its rescue rationale is also gone: E042 and E045 already recovered the bs-1536 deficit (margin 0.38 pp), and E046 showed the bs-1536 loss does not respond to Muon tuning. Re-propose ghost BN only as a companion to bs 2048 if I057 lands in its 0.15-0.35 pp keep-and-pair band.

structured_output.summary:
The tip is E045: 0.7568 accuracy at 5.464 s, about 0.38 pp above the gate. The fastest feasible run so far is still E041 at 5.42 s, with 0.03 pp to spare. The clear next step is to spend E045's margin on E044's 28 px stage, which cost -0.23 pp for -4.4% time, a cheap trade at ~0.052 pp per 1% (I061, priority 5, expected ~5.22 s / ~0.7545).

I062 is a fallback: if the 28 px stage fails, trim 0.25 epoch from the 32 px phase instead (-3.9%), pre-registered in I053.

The remaining slots go to untested levers:
- H1.8.2: drop translate-2 entirely.
- H1.7.1: BN-bias lr x128, since the head result (x0.5 hurt, x2 helped) says the SGD group is under-driven.
- H2.5.1: default-mode compile. This one is mainly a guard on build time: curriculum and batch-size variants keep adding compiled graphs against the 600 s build limit.

I dropped I059 (ghost BN) because its time cost beats its expected gain, and the bs-1536 loss it was meant to fix has already been recovered.

The queue now holds 8 ideas: I054, I057, I058 and I061-I065. I060 (20 px first stage) is still running. If it is kept, I061 rebases onto it.
